# forum-dl upstream engine

Upstream: https://github.com/mikwielgus/forum-dl
Revision: **f2168a89fc2a8b713626700d1e638016ff67623d**, package 0.3.0.
License: MIT, copyright 2022 Mikolaj Wielgus. Original license: `upstream/LICENSE`.

`upstream/` is the complete unchanged Python package. `upstream/SHA256SUMS` records its bytes. `public/forum-dl/forum_dl-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl` is built from that tree plus the explicitly documented source corrections in `patches/` using `uv run --no-project vendor/forum-dl/build-runtime.py`. The previous HN/Discourse TypeScript translations have been removed. All eleven upstream extractor modules execute in bundled Pyodide 0.29.3/Python 3.13: Hacker News, Hyperkitty, Pipermail, Hypermail, XenForo, vBulletin, ProBoards, Invision, Discourse, Simple Machines and phpBB.

## Runtime boundaries

- `runtime.ts` loads only packaged interpreter and dependency assets. `packages.json` records dependency URLs and SHA-256 digests; `prepare-runtime.mjs` reproduces downloaded assets and verifies those hashes. lxml and regex use the actual Pyodide binary builds, Pydantic is the real 1.10.26 pure Python release, and BeautifulSoup/dateparser retain their upstream implementations. Requests and its pure Python dependencies are shared with `public/gallery-dl`. SSL comes from the shared Pyodide assets. `cchardet` is only an optional BeautifulSoup accelerator, never imported by forum-dl; BeautifulSoup uses its bundled supported charset-normalizer dependency. Native WARC output is disabled because the shared recorder owns WARC creation.
- `bridge.py` mounts the shared `vendor/python/requests.py` Requests adapter on the forum-dl Session. Gallery and papers use that same streaming, cookie and response implementation. HTTP acquisition uses the shared recorder and browser credentials. Offline transport resolves saved WACZ responses and has no network fallback. Session cache and already-visited rules, exact detector order, all parsing and pagination stay upstream.
- `pipeline.py` supplies the upstream `FileWriter` serialization extension point. Upstream Writer still owns board/thread/post traversal and downloads every selected File through the same Session. Its model objects are transient; the WACZ stores original responses and hook references only. Embedded file bodies already occur in source markup and are not duplicated in derived metadata. The same writer reconstructs metadata offline.
- A hook can report success only after a second isolated interpreter reconstructs identical boards, threads, posts and files through capture-only response reads. The offline viewer also runs in an isolated worker and has no HTTP fallback.
- Requests use one attempt. Browser timeouts and explicit request/byte budgets terminate incomplete work instead of hiding failures with retries. Upstream sometimes catches extraction errors; its warning diagnostics are retained and mark traversal incomplete. Missing null HN items retain upstream semantics.
- Browser-managed authentication, TLS, redirects and headers have the capabilities and limitations of the shared recorder. Browser Fetch follows redirects and only the terminal supplemental exchange is preserved unless intermediate responses were observed in the page. Native socket proxying, client TLS certificates and filesystem credential imports are not implemented. CLI mailbox output/resume is outside this WACZ presentation boundary.

## Verification and limits

`tests/forum-upstream-live.test.ts` runs the packaged corpus natively against public Hacker News, Discourse, HyperKitty, Hypermail, Pipermail and phpBB pages, captures those same pages through the extension UI, exports/deletes/reimports its WACZ with Chromium offline, and compares complete posts, threads and files against the native run. It also checks all seventeen classes across eleven module families, zero live HTTP during offline derivation, no duplicate original WARC bodies, and exact SHA-256 for every indexed payload resolved through production replay. The phpBB case checks one source request per explicit forum-dl User-Agent and an original image rendered offline. `native-reference.py` supplies the native comparison using the identical upstream wheel. Offline native model records are compared using the canonical viewer’s Download JSONL action. The viewer uses the vendored ArchiveBox forumdl `full.html` and `card.html`; its original script is compiled in `src/ui/forum-template.js`. Only transient model input, original WACZ image URLs, output actions and native path-based reply relationships adapt to the extension. No extra metadata table or explanatory UI is added.

Bundling all extractors does not establish live compatibility for every site. Current native probes: the public Python mm3_test HyperKitty thread produces two posts; the Luanti phpBB thread produces 76 posts and 78 File objects from 45 original responses; the Hypermail 1998 fixture produces 15 posts after routing its legacy date strings through the existing dateparser dependency; phpbb.com and simplemachines.org fixtures present access challenges. Those upstream/site failures are not replaced with partial hand-written parsers and must not be represented as verified coverage. HN feed caching and Discourse nested category/pagination regressions are corrected by the documented source patch, with real red native acceptance evidence. No site parser is replaced by a TypeScript approximation.

Additional real probes are not counted as complete coverage: the Pipermail OSI example passes 22 posts; upstream XenForo, vBulletin and Invision example URLs serve Cloudflare access challenges. Accessible Delphi-Praxis Invision list markup and EEVblog Simple Machines category text expose native selector/type errors. SolarPanelTalk vBulletin parses nine posts but native Requests rejects embedded data-URI images; Detroit Sports XenForo and ProBoards examples include unavailable remote images. The engine correctly reports those incomplete traversals.

`0003-identify-phpbb-before-construction.patch` requires an actual phpBB body identifier or phpBB project link before constructing the extractor. Upstream previously accepted any `html[dir]`, including Wikimedia Commons 404 pages, then failed resolving an invented forum root. Native Commons red/green evidence confirms no detector now matches; real HTTP errors remain errors.
